prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an outdoor desert campsite where the camera wearer turns and looks up from a foreground grate table and camp stove (0.4–1.0 m away, within arm's reach at the bottom of frames 1–2) toward a seated group and a standing man. In frames 1–3, a person in a blue shirt sits on a cooler about 1.8–2.5 m ahead with their back turned, partially occluding three seated people behind and to their right (3–4.5 m away, spaced 1–1.5 m apart in a circle facing inward, none looking at the camera wearer), while a standing man faces left about 3.5–4 m to the left in frame 3 with his legs partly cut off at the top of frames 1–2 and a tent 8–10 m behind him. As the camera pans right in frames 4–5, the seated group shifts to the far left background (3.5–5 m away) and another standing man wearing a cap appears on the right at 0.8–1.2 m, facing left in profile and reaching within arm's length of items on the foreground table while cropped below the waist. Compared to the cluttered RGB image with harsh shadows, the depth map clearly separates the foreground stove, water bottle, and right-side man's silhouette from the mid-ground campers and distant canyon walls (>50 m, black). However, the depth map is unreliable where it blurs the open mesh of the foreground table into a solid slab, flattens depth differences between the blue-shirted person and the foreground table in frame 3, and loses fine contours of folding chairs and background limbs.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates selected people and foreground objects across the camera wearer's pan from the camp table (0.4–1.0 m below and in front) to the wider campsite, though most of the scene remains unlabelled. In frame 1, it detects only a small fragment of the seated blue-shirted person at 2 m (mislabelled as a suitcase), and in frame 2 it merges the foreground table, stove, water bottle (within the wearer's 0.5–0.8 m reach), cooler, and the blue-shirted person at 2 m into a single oversized mask mislabelled as a motorcycle, with a small table edge on the right mislabelled as a snowboard. In frame 3, it segments the standing man 3.5–4 m to the left (facing left, holding an item within his arm's reach while a tent behind him is mislabelled as an umbrella) and separates the cluster of four seated people 2–4.5 m to the right (spaced 1–1.5 m apart, facing away or inward rather than at the wearer, with the blue-shirted person in front partially occluding those behind). As the camera turns right in frames 4–5, a man in a cap enters on the right at 0.8–1.2 m (facing left and looking down toward the table within his arm's reach, cropped at the waist), while the background seated group shifts to the left edge and becomes increasingly occluded. While the masks in frames 3–4 help distinguish overlapping individuals in the distant seated group that blend into the bright terrain and shadows in RGB, the map is highly unreliable due to severe class mislabelling in frames 1–2, completely missing the people in frames 1–2 and the background group in frame 5, and misclassifying a foreground table object as a person in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1–4 and only detects a single partial body skeleton in frame 5 for the standing man in the cap positioned 0.8–1.0 m to the right of the camera wearer. In frame 5, the yellow upper-body and arm keypoints show him standing above the foreground table, facing left in profile with his head tilted downward toward the tabletop rather than looking at the camera wearer, while his lower body is out of view below the bottom frame edge. His left arm extends forward and downward with the wrist near the bottom-right edge, placing his hands within arm's reach (about 0.4–0.5 m) of the objects on the foreground table and roughly 0.6–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer. This skeleton makes the exact shoulder-elbow-wrist angles of his reaching posture easier to read than in the heavily shadowed RGB torso, where dark clothing obscures his arm segments. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because it fails to detect the same man in frame 4, misses all other nearby and mid-ground people (located 1.8–5 m away across the five frames) as well as the camera wearer's own reach, and omits the magenta hand keypoints entirely even in frame 5.
